name: ping keeps the setup contract
why: The supplied adapter must still answer {"status":"ready"}.

name: dsu two merges then a bridge
why: {0,1} -> 4 comps, largest 2; {2,3} -> 3 comps, largest 2; 1-3 joins both pairs -> {0,1,2,3}: 2 comps, largest 4; self-union 4-4 and repeated union 0-3 change nothing.

name: dsu single vertex self-union
why: A self-union never changes the partition; the only set has size 1.

name: dsu vertices but no operations
why: No initial state is reported, so zero operations give an empty list.

name: dsu star growth with reversed repeat
why: Each of the first three unions adds one vertex to 0's set; 3-2 is already connected.

name: kruskal single isolated vertex
why: One isolate is one component; the forest has n-c = 0 edges.

name: prim single isolated vertex
why: Same graph as the Kruskal case.

name: kruskal negative self-loops are never selected
why: Loops join nothing, so both vertices stay isolated even though the loop weights are negative.

name: prim negative self-loops are never selected
why: Same graph as the Kruskal case.

name: kruskal all-negative weights
why: Ascending: -10 (0-3), -3 (0-1), -2 (1-2) join all four vertices; -1 and 5 would close cycles. -10-3-2 = -15.

name: prim all-negative weights
why: Same graph; the optimum is unique: {0-3, 0-1, 1-2}.

name: kruskal parallel edges keep the cheapest
why: Exactly one edge is needed; IDs 1 and 2 tie at weight 2, either is valid.

name: prim parallel edges keep the cheapest
why: Same graph as the Kruskal case.

name: kruskal two components plus an isolate
why: Components {0,1,2}, {3,4}, {5}; triangle MST = 1+2, plus 7 = 10; n-c = 3 edges.

name: prim two components plus an isolate
why: Prim must restart at 3 and again at 5.

name: kruskal cycle of 1e9 edges (total beyond 32 bits)
why: Any 4 of the 5 equal cycle edges form an MST; 4 * 1e9 = 4e9 > 2^31-1.

name: prim complete K4 of -1e9 edges (negative 64-bit total)
why: A spanning tree of K4 has 3 edges, all -1e9: -3e9 < -2^31.

name: scc two cycles, a sink and duplicate cross pairs
why: {0,1,2} and {3,4} are cycles, 5 is a sink. Cross pairs: A->B (from 2-3 and 1-3, reported once), B->C (4-5), A->C (0-5).

name: scc one big cycle
why: Every vertex reaches every other; condensation is empty.

name: scc DAG with a duplicate edge
why: No cycles, so three singleton SCCs and three distinct condensation pairs (0-2 appears twice in input, once in output).

name: scc self-loops only
why: A self-loop is internal to its singleton SCC; no condensation pairs.

name: scc single vertex
why: One isolated vertex is one SCC.

name: topo diamond
why: 0 before 1 and 2, both before 3; [0,1,2,3] and [0,2,1,3] are both valid.

name: topo cycle in a separate component
why: 2 -> 3 -> 2 is a cycle even though it is not reachable from vertex 0; order must be [].

name: topo edge to a finished vertex is not a cycle
why: DFS from 0 finishes 1 first, then 2 -> 1 hits a finished vertex: a cross edge, not a back edge. Valid order: [0,2,1].

name: topo single vertex
why: The only order is [0].

name: topo cycle closed by the last edge
dag negative edge beats a direct edge
why: 0->1->2->3 costs 2+3-4 = 1 < 10 (direct edge 0). Parents: 1 via edge 1, 2 via edge 2, 3 via edge 3.

name: dag source in the middle, no relaxation from unreachable vertices
why: Only 3 is reachable from 2 (edge 2, weight -2). Vertex 0 is unreachable, so edge 3 (0->3) must not be relaxed.

name: dag cycle unreachable from the source
why: 2 -> 3 -> 4 -> 2 is a cycle elsewhere in the graph: the whole graph is not a DAG.

name: dag parallel tied cheapest edges
why: Best weight -3 is achieved by edge 1 and edge 2; either parent_edge[1] is valid, edge 0 is not.

name: dag distance -1 and 0 are real costs
why: -1 and 0 are finite distances, not 'unreachable' markers.

name: dag negative 64-bit chain
why: -3e9 does not fit 32 bits.

name: dag unreachable self-loop
why: A self-loop is a directed cycle, even when unreachable from the source.
